title: Flow Builder Wiring Basics: Nodes, Handles and Connectors
description: A flow is a set of nodes on a canvas, joined by lines. One node sends a message, another waits, another checks a condition, and the lines decide what runs after what.
html:
A flow is a set of nodes on a canvas, joined by lines. One node sends a message, another waits, another checks a condition, and the lines decide what runs after what.

Open the Flow builder

Choose Create automation → Flow builder. Start with the Begin when… block and add a trigger, then connect it to your first step. Free accounts can save and preview a draft; publishing custom flows requires Pro or Business.

Adding a node

Click + on the canvas, choose a node type, configure it in the editor and connect its output to the next step. Message options include text, buttons, product cards, carousels and collecting information.

The node types

  • Trigger: starts the flow from an Instagram interaction.
  • Send message: sends text or a linked message.
  • Collect email, phone or information: waits for an answer.
  • Action: adds or removes a tag, sets a field or sends an external request.
  • Conditions: checks a value and branches.
  • Delay: waits before continuing.
  • Randomizer: splits traffic between two paths.
  • Finish: ends the flow.

AP3K does not have a Payment node. Send an existing HTTPS checkout link in a message instead.

Connecting nodes

Drag an output handle to the next node. You can also choose the destination in the node editor. Conditions have Yes and No branches, randomizers have two percentage branches, and questions have one branch per choice. Collection steps have a response path and a skip path.

Leave an output set to Finish here to end that path. Check every branch before publishing. Unreachable steps and automatic loops without a customer response are rejected.

Review the canvas

Use zoom and fit controls to see the whole flow. After deleting a node, check its neighbouring connections. Preview every route, then test a published flow from a second Instagram account. Comment flows require an opening message and button so the contact can start the messaging window.

title: Trigger Node: Start a Flow in the Flow Builder
description:
Every flow has to start somewhere, and that’s what a Trigger is. It’s the event
that wakes your automation up and gets it moving.
html:
Every flow has to start somewhere, and that’s what a Trigger is. It’s the event that wakes your automation up and gets it moving.

No trigger, no flow. It’s step one, always.

Setting one up

  1. Click + New Trigger in the Begin when… block
  2. Pick the event that should kick things off
  3. Set any conditions the trigger needs
  4. Connect it to your first step

Available triggers

Trigger Fires when…
User comments on your Post or Reel Someone comments on a post or reel
User replies to your Story Someone replies to your story
User sends a message Someone DMs you
User mentions you in a Story You get story-mentioned
User shares a post or reel Someone shares your content via DM

Narrowing a trigger

A trigger doesn’t have to fire on everything. Once you’ve picked the event, set the condition that goes with it — a User sends a message trigger can listen for any message, or only ones containing a keyword like hello, exactly like the keyword triggers in a basic automation.

The node shows what it settled on: the event on top, the condition underneath.

Pro Tip

Start with the event you can test yourself. Comment on your own post from a second account, or DM yourself the keyword, and watch the flow run before you point it at anything that matters.

Where to go next

With the trigger in place, drag its Then handle to the first real step — usually a Send message node.

Comment flows need an opening message and button before the full conversation can proceed. Test with a second account and use a post owned by the connected Instagram account.

title: Send Message Node: Layouts and Content Blocks
description: This is how your flow talks to people. Add a message step, pick the content type and write the message in the editor.
html:
This is how your flow talks to people. Add a message step, pick the content type and write the message in the editor.

Content types

StepUse it for
Send messageText and up to three HTTPS link buttons.
Message with buttonsUp to three choices that route to separate steps.
Product cardAn image, title, subtitle and link buttons.
Product carouselUp to ten scrollable product cards.
Collect email, phone or informationA prompt that waits for the contact’s reply.

Connect separate steps to send several pieces of content. File attachments in the basic automation editor are separate from these flow node types.

Setup

  1. Add the message step.
  2. Write your text and give the step a useful label.
  3. Add your destination links, using HTTPS.
  4. Connect the next step or choose Finish here.
  5. Preview the conversation and test the links on a phone.

A plain flow message supports up to 1,000 characters. Link button labels support up to 20 characters. Product card titles and subtitles support up to 80 characters each.

Using collected values

A stored custom field can be inserted with a token such as {{first_name}}. Collect or set that field before using it: unavailable values render empty. Preview and test the result rather than assuming every contact has the same data.

Waiting for an answer

A collection step pauses until the person replies. Connect its valid response path to the next step and configure the skip path. Email and phone collection validates the answer before advancing and stores the details against the responding contact.

Keep each burst to at most six messages between customer replies or delays. A flow is a conversation, not a reason to send every available message at once.

title: Action Node: Tags, Custom Fields and API Requests
description: While other nodes control where a flow goes, actions change what AP3K knows about a contact or send data to an external service.
html:
While other nodes control where a flow goes, actions change what AP3K knows about a contact or send data to an external service.

Setup

Add an action from the canvas, select its type and configure it in the node editor. Connect another action after it when several operations need to run in order.

Available actions

ActionWhat it does
Contact tagAdds or removes a tag.
Set custom fieldSaves a field value for later messages and conditions.
External request / ZapierSends a JSON POST request to a public HTTPS webhook.

AP3K does not provide a Delete contact flow action. Manage contacts from the Contacts page instead.

Setting a field

Enter the field name and the value to save. Use the same name in later collection steps, conditions and message tokens. Instagram profile fields are reserved and cannot be overwritten with a custom-field action.

Tags versus custom fields

Tags are labels, and a contact can have several. Custom fields hold values such as language, membership tier or campaign source. Use tags to segment; use fields to store.

Sending an external request

Use a public HTTPS URL on port 443 and a JSON object body. Variables belong inside JSON string values. This action uses POST and does not offer custom request headers. Do not paste credentials into a message or a public link.

The label mentions Zapier because a compatible webhook can receive the request; AP3K does not supply the separate native Zapier app described by some migration guides.

Example flow

Incoming DM → Collect email → Set campaign field → Add interested tag → Send confirmation. Review the contact record after testing to confirm that the right person’s data was updated.

title: Conditions Node: Branch a Flow with Yes and No Paths
description: A Conditions node checks a value and sends the contact down one of two paths: Yes when it matches, or No when it does not.
html:
A Conditions node checks a value and sends the contact down one of two paths: Yes when it matches, or No when it does not.

Setup

Add a Conditions step, choose the condition type, select a comparison and enter a value where required. Wire both branches to their next steps.

Available condition types

  • If user followed me.
  • If business follows user.
  • Verified on Instagram.
  • Followers count.
  • Opened a tracked link.
  • Contact email or phone.
  • A custom field.

Comparisons include Equals, Does not equal, Contains, Greater than, Less than and Has a value. Choose one that fits the data being checked.

Collect the data first

Email, phone and custom fields should be collected or set before the check. Use Has a value when you want to skip a collection prompt for someone whose information is already stored.

Instagram profile conditions are verified when the step runs. Unavailable profile data does not qualify, so provide a useful fallback path.

Example

Trigger → Conditions: Contact email has a value → Yes: send the resource → No: collect email, then send the resource.

An unwired branch ends the path. Test both outcomes so a missing field does not silently strand a contact.

title: Delay Node: Pause a Flow Before the Next Step
description: The Delay node pauses a flow before moving on. Use it to space messages or wait before a follow-up, while respecting Instagram’s reply window.
html:
The Delay node pauses a flow before moving on. Use it to space messages or wait before a follow-up, while respecting Instagram’s reply window.

Setup

  1. Add a Delay step.
  2. Enter the duration and choose seconds, minutes, hours or days.
  3. Connect the next step.
  4. Preview the path and test its timing from another account.

How timing works

The wait is saved before the flow pauses. A first short delay of up to 30 seconds can resume in the background. Longer waits and recovery depend on the scheduler, so the selected duration is a minimum wait rather than a promise of delivery at an exact second.

Nothing downstream runs until the delay is due and the flow remains eligible to continue. An unavailable scheduler can prevent publication or postpone delivery.

Instagram’s reply window

Scheduled flow messages only send while the Instagram reply window is open. AP3K checks the conversation window again before sending; a wait beyond the current window is cancelled rather than used to bypass it. A duration field accepting days does not guarantee that a message can be delivered days later.

Use this for

  • A brief pause between related messages.
  • A timely follow-up after the contact has engaged.
  • Waiting before checking a tracked-link condition.

For a missing delayed DM, check the automation is active, the account is connected and the reply window is still open before changing the duration.

title: Randomizer Node: Split a Flow Across Random Paths
description: The Randomizer splits contacts between two paths by chance, in the proportions you set. The choice is not based on what you know about a contact.
html:
The Randomizer splits contacts between two paths by chance, in the proportions you set. The choice is not based on what you know about a contact.

Setup

  1. Add a Randomizer node.
  2. Set First branch probability using the slider.
  3. Connect the first percentage output to one next step.
  4. Connect the second percentage output to another step.

The first branch can be 1–99%. The second is calculated automatically as the remainder, so the total is always 100%.

Percentages are odds, not quotas

A 50/50 split does not alternate contacts. Each draw can take either branch, so a small sample may look uneven. Compare results over enough conversations to avoid drawing conclusions from a handful of people.

Returning contacts

AP3K saves the selected outcome before sending so a retry does not redraw that step. It does not offer a separate sticky-assignment or “Pick a random path every time” toggle. Do not assume a returning contact is permanently assigned to one variation across new flow runs.

Example: compare two openers

Incoming keyword → Randomizer at 50% → First branch: short welcome → Second branch: detailed welcome. Send each branch to an appropriate next step and change only the wording you want to compare.

Wire both paths

An unwired output ends the flow for contacts assigned to it. Make each variation easy to recognize during testing. AP3K’s randomizer has two outputs; there is no four-variation editor or payment-gateway experiment node.

title: Payments in a Flow: Send a Checkout Link
description: AP3K does not currently include a Payment or Collect payment flow node. You can send a checkout link created with your existing store or payment provider.
html:
AP3K does not currently include a Payment or Collect payment flow node. You can send a checkout link created with your existing store or payment provider.

Send a checkout link

  1. Create the checkout or product link with your payment provider.
  2. Add a Send message or Product card step in AP3K.
  3. Write a clear description of the offer.
  4. Add an HTTPS button such as Buy now pointing to the checkout.
  5. Test the button and checkout with your provider’s testing tools.

What AP3K does and does not track

AP3K can track a click on a tracked link. Clicking a link is not proof of payment. Check payment completion in your provider or store.

There is no built-in gateway-connection wizard, dynamic payment-link creation or Payment successful/Payment failed branch in AP3K. Do not promise automatic paid-only delivery based solely on a link click.

A supported sales flow

Incoming DM → Ask which product the contact needs → Send the matching product card and checkout link. Use your store’s normal fulfilment process after a confirmed purchase.

Related steps

See Send message for link buttons and product cards, or Conditions for supported contact checks.

headings.text: What AP3K does and does not track

title: AI Flow Builder: Build a Flow from a Prompt
description: Describe the automation in plain words and let the Flow Assistant prepare an editable draft. It builds ordinary flow nodes that you can inspect and change.
html:
Describe the automation in plain words and let the Flow Assistant prepare an editable draft. It builds ordinary flow nodes that you can inspect and change.

Open the assistant

Choose Create automation → AI assisted flow builder, or open the Flow Assistant from the flow editor. AI flow generation requires Pro or Business and uses your AI allowance.

How it works

  1. Describe the trigger, message, desired branches and destination links.
  2. Generate the draft and read the assistant’s summary.
  3. Inspect the trigger and each node on the canvas.
  4. Replace missing destinations or placeholders.
  5. Preview the conversation, then save or publish when ready.

Generation prepares a draft; it does not send messages or publish the automation for you.

Example prompts

  • “When someone comments LINK, send an opener and then my download link after they respond.”
  • “When someone sends pricing, tag them as a lead and send this pricing page.”
  • “Collect email addresses from people who reply FREEBIE, then send my resource.”
  • “Ask whether the contact is a creator or a brand and send each answer to a different message.”

Review before publishing

Check message wording, selected post, links, conditions and actions. If a destination was not provided, the assistant may leave a placeholder that must be replaced. It cannot create unsupported payment nodes, send outbound email or invent an integration.

Use a second Instagram account for a real test after publishing. Draft preview helps review the logic but does not prove that an external API or live Instagram delivery succeeded.

title: Flow Analytics: See How Your Automations Perform
description: Look at the results after publishing to see whether people trigger your flow and use its links. AP3K provides automation-level analytics and account performance views.
html:
Look at the results after publishing to see whether people trigger your flow and use its links. AP3K provides automation-level analytics and account performance views.

The Automations list

Find the flow in Automations and check whether it is active. Open its analytics to review Hits and Clicks, daily activity and available click-country data. Select the intended Instagram account before comparing results.

Account performance

The Instagram account performance view provides account-level context. Its totals are broader than a single flow, so use the automation’s own analytics when evaluating one campaign.

Reading the result

  • Few hits: confirm the selected post and keyword match what people actually send.
  • Hits but few clicks: verify delivery, then review the DM, link destination and call to action.
  • A branch appears unused: test its condition and confirm the required contact data exists.

A draft has not sent live messages. Pausing an automation stops new processing; it does not erase historical results.

Compare one change at a time

Change a message, trigger or link individually so you can judge its effect. AP3K does not provide the source documentation’s per-node conversion counters or payment-success analytics. Use live test conversations to inspect individual branches.

headings.text: Compare one change at a time

title: Flow Templates: Start From a Ready-Made Automation
description: Start from an AP3K automation template, customize its trigger and messages, review the required plan, then publish and test your flow.
html:
An empty canvas is the slowest way to start. The template gallery holds ready-made automations, and the Flow tab filters it down to the ones that open on the flow canvas rather than in the simple editor. Choose a template, customize its settings and review it before publishing.

Opening the template gallery

Click + New automation, then Browse templates at the foot of the dialog, and switch to the Flow tab. The Basic tab beside it holds the post, story and chat templates; some of these use the flow editor for their conversation steps.

Making a template yours

A template is a starting point, not a finished automation. Once it opens in the Flow builder, go through it the same way you’d review your own work:

  • The trigger — point it at your post, reel or keyword. This is the part a template can’t guess.
  • The message content — replace the placeholder copy and links with yours, and check it sounds like you.
  • Any conditions and actions — tags and custom fields in a template refer to names that may not exist in your account yet.

Then publish, and test it from a second account before you point real traffic at it.

Pro Tip

Templates are also the fastest way to read a good flow. Open one close to what you want, see how it’s wired, and you’ll know how to build the next one from scratch.

Some templates open in the flow editor even when listed under Basic. Free users can save and preview flow drafts; publishing custom flows requires Pro or Business. Replace all example destinations before publishing.

title: DM Queue
description: AP3K stores delayed deliveries, scheduled follow-ups and waiting flow sessions so eligible work can continue later. There is no separate In queue panel in the AP3K sidebar.
html:
AP3K stores delayed deliveries, scheduled follow-ups and waiting flow sessions so eligible work can continue later. There is no separate In queue panel in the AP3K sidebar.

What waits for delivery?

A configured delay waits until its due time. A follow-up waits for its schedule and conditions. A collection step waits for the contact’s reply. These are different reasons for a message not appearing immediately.

Immediate and scheduled messages

Do not assume every immediate message passes through a visible account-wide queue. Scheduled work is stored durably and processed by delivery workers or the scheduler. Eligibility is checked again when it resumes.

What can stop a waiting message?

  • The automation is inactive or archived.
  • The Instagram connection requires attention.
  • The contact or conversation no longer meets the conditions.
  • The reply window has expired.
  • An API or delivery error prevents sending.

Stored work is not a guarantee of eventual delivery. Expired or ineligible work can be cancelled, and ambiguous failures are not blindly replayed.

Check delivery

Review the automation status, the recipient’s Inbox conversation and account connection. For delay-specific checks, see Delay node. For general problems, see Automation not working.

headings.text: What can stop a waiting message?

title: How the DM Queue Works
description: When an AP3K step is scheduled for later, its due time and state are stored before processing pauses. A worker resumes eligible work when it becomes due.
html:
When an AP3K step is scheduled for later, its due time and state are stored before processing pauses. A worker resumes eligible work when it becomes due.

The trip a scheduled message makes

  1. An interaction matches an active automation.
  2. A delay or follow-up creates waiting work.
  3. A worker claims that work when it is due.
  4. AP3K checks that the automation, account and conversation are still eligible.
  5. The message is sent, cancelled or marked failed according to the outcome.

Two kinds of waiting

Waiting for time: a delay or follow-up has not reached its due date. Waiting for a person: a flow needs an answer or button interaction before it can continue. Neither means that the message is ready to send immediately.

Timing and recovery

A saved due time is a minimum wait. Worker availability and scheduler cadence can add latency. Durable state allows recovery after an interrupted worker, but AP3K avoids automatically replaying an ambiguous external send that might duplicate a DM.

Messages can expire

Instagram’s reply window still applies. Expired flow sessions are cancelled, and delayed jobs may be cancelled when the conversation has moved on or the automation is no longer active. There is no promise that a queued message waits forever.

Common questions

Can I buy faster delivery? A subscription does not bypass Instagram’s limits.

Where is the queue count? AP3K does not expose the source site’s In queue panel or account-wide messages-per-minute readout.

How do I investigate a missing message? Check the Inbox, active automation, selected account, configured wait and any connection or publishing error.

headings.text: The trip a scheduled message makes

title: DM Rate Limits and Throttling
description: Instagram controls which messages its API will accept. Account restrictions, usage limits and the conversation window can affect delivery independently of your AP3K subscription.
html:
Instagram controls which messages its API will accept. Account restrictions, usage limits and the conversation window can affect delivery independently of your AP3K subscription.

What rate limiting means

A rate-limit response means the platform is restricting API activity. Repeatedly triggering the same automation does not raise that limit and can make diagnosis harder. Inspect the reported error and the account’s connection state first.

No speed override

AP3K does not offer a user-configurable DM sending rate or a paid priority lane. It also does not display the source documentation’s Smart Queue Control panel. Avoid treating an example rate such as 60 DMs/min as a guaranteed AP3K delivery speed.

Reduce unnecessary activity

  • Use a specific keyword when only interested commenters need the response.
  • Review overlapping automations on the same post.
  • Use the one-DM-per-user setting where appropriate.
  • Keep flows concise and test with a small audience before a launch.

Distinguish a wait from a failure

A configured delay has a due time; a collection step waits for an answer; a failed API request needs investigation. These are not interchangeable. A long wait can also cross the reply window, preventing later delivery.

Further help

Review Instagram messaging API errors and Slow DM delivery. Platform limits can change; use Meta’s current documentation when investigating a specific API limit rather than an old numeric table.

headings.text: Distinguish a wait from a failure

title: Check Your DM Queue Status
description: AP3K does not currently include an In queue panel with pending counts, delivery speed or queue controls. Use the automation and conversation views to check what happened.
html:
AP3K does not currently include an In queue panel with pending counts, delivery speed or queue controls. Use the automation and conversation views to check what happened.

Check the right account

Select the Instagram account that owns the automation. Confirm it is connected and that no reconnection warning is shown.

Check the automation

  1. Find it in Automations and confirm it is active.
  2. Review its trigger, selected post and keyword.
  3. Check whether a delay, collection step or follow-up condition intentionally waits.
  4. Open its analytics to see whether the trigger received hits.

Check the conversation

Open the contact in Inbox. Compare the latest inbound interaction with the expected step. A flow waiting for an answer will not advance merely because time has passed. A delay cannot extend an expired Instagram reply window.

If delivery still looks stuck

Test once from a second Instagram account, note the automation and approximate time, and review any visible error. Use Automation not working for the next checks. Do not repeatedly publish duplicate automations to force a message through.

title: Pause, Clear or Cancel Queued DMs
description: AP3K does not have account-wide queue pause, resume or clear buttons. To stop a campaign, turn off the relevant automation from the Automations list.
html:
AP3K does not have account-wide queue pause, resume or clear buttons. To stop a campaign, turn off the relevant automation from the Automations list.

Pause an automation

  1. Select the Instagram account that owns it.
  2. Open Automations and find the campaign.
  3. Turn the automation off.
  4. Make and review your changes before activating it again.

Turning it off prevents new processing. Delivery workers also check active status before resuming eligible work. A message already handed to Instagram cannot be recalled this way.

What happens to scheduled work

Inactive or ineligible work can be cancelled when a worker checks it. Do not treat turning an automation off as a temporary account-wide queue hold with a guaranteed replay later. Reactivating it does not guarantee that previously cancelled messages will be sent.

If the wrong message was published

Deactivate the automation first, correct the content and inspect affected conversations in Inbox. Review the trigger and test the replacement before restarting. There is no Clear queue command in AP3K to cancel all account messages with one click.

Keep public replies without a DM

For a basic post automation, use its supported DM controls when you want public replies without direct messages. See Disable direct messages for the relevant editor.

headings.text: If the wrong message was published
Keep public replies without a DM
